source.title: Back into Plato's Cave: Examining Cross-modal Representational Convergence at Scale
source.authors: A. S. Koepke; D. Zverev; Shiry Ginosar; Alexei A. Efros

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly re-examines cross-modal alignment and argues that the evidence for convergence is partial: fine-grained mutual-kNN alignment falls with gallery density, performance trends saturate for recent models, and results depend on the metric and correspondence structure.
record.gate_note: The paper measures cross-modal and same-modality representation similarity, evaluates alignment against language-model capability, and compares outcomes across metrics and data conditions. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. Reported layer-search choices and captioning prompt instructions are not results.
record.test_reason: The study reruns Huh et al.'s mutual-kNN text-image alignment and its capability-trend analysis, then extends both: denser galleries, 36 recent LLMs, non-bijective data, RSA/CKA, and ImageNet ceilings. Its own numbers bear on V1/V2 (whether alignment keeps rising with LLM capability), V6 (dependence on k, gallery, metric and correspondence structure) and V7 (incomplete alignment and plateau). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that image and text models share coarse, category-level structure but organise fine-grained structure differently. They find no evidence of convergence to a shared representation. They treat the drop under dense galleries as genuine organisational divergence. They treat the drop under non-bijective data as a limitation of the mutual-kNN protocol. Saturation of the capability trend holds for base-only models and under calibrated RSA/CKA.
record.recipe_differences: Follows Huh et al.'s mutual-kNN setup and trend analysis, but extends it to larger galleries, more recent models, non-bijective correspondences, other modalities, ImageNet, and additional metrics including RSA and CKA.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment results depend on neighborhood size k, gallery density, one-to-one versus many-to-many correspondence, metric choice (mutual kNN versus RSA/CKA), benchmark used to score language capability, and caption length.
record.problems: The trend check holds the vision encoder fixed and the authors leave joint scaling of both modalities to future work. The text-video and text-audio analyses use narrower model and gallery coverage than the text-image analysis. Some results are presented in figures without exact numeric values in the text. The paper notes that residual near-duplicate samples remain after deduplication.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported outcomes were omitted from the selected claim-relevant findings. Figure-only model-pair and gallery-scale values were not transcribed when the text did not give an explicit numerical result.

untested.parts: Only the LLM side varies against fixed DINOv2 encoders. There is no joint scaling of both modalities, and architecture, objective and data are not varied systematically.
The vision side is not scaled jointly with the language side. The four DINOv2 sizes are used only as repeated fixed encoders.
Not tested: no mapping, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired-translation experiments.
Not tested: no feature- or circuit-level universality analysis.
The causal part (shared data or objectives explain the overlap) is not tested. Authors only remark that coarse overlap is expected from overlapping internet data.

missing.what: The original WIT-1024 k=10 trend replicates. This is the basis for the V2 supports label in the coarse regime.
Text-video and text-audio results. Fixed-k alignment drops with gallery size while k=n/100 stays stable. The capability trend is weak for video and flat for audio.
Split of recent models into base-only and post-trained. R² is negative on all benchmarks, including HellaSwag (−0.231) and Wikitext (−0.266) for base-only models.
The fixed-k drop persists across other model pairs: DINOv2-giant/OpenLlama-13b, CLIP, Pixio, Gemma-7B, Mistral-7B.
The drop persists after layer re-selection per scale and after recaptioning with 500-word captions.
Non-synthetic WIT many-to-many data: mutual kNN drops as images per caption or captions per image go from 1 to 5.
Within-class cross-modal RSA is 77–85% of the ceiling. Between-class RSA is 0.79 vs 0.94. On WIT-1024 with rich captions, cross-modal RSA saturates at 0.64 while the language ceiling is 0.92–0.99.
Unimodal cross-family pair DINOv2 vs CLIP-B/16 stays stable under densification.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 labels were limits_scope, but the results match what V7, a challenge version, says (incomplete alignment, plateau), so they are relabelled supports. V1 is tested only through the cross-modal LLM-capability axis against fixed DINOv2 encoders. Several partial states were upgraded to observed because the drop or incompleteness is the full effect V6/V7 describe.

versions.untested_parts: Does not jointly scale both modalities or systematically vary architecture, objective, and training data while measuring alignment.
The trend checks vary language-model capability while holding the vision encoder fixed; joint improvement of both modalities is left to future work.
No comparison across random seeds of the same architecture.
No test of mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired interchangeability.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.

Metric and input dependence are tested for the reported text-image, text-video, text-audio, and ImageNet settings; other similarity measures, settings, and out-of-distribution inputs are not comprehensively tested.
The study measures incomplete alignment and saturation, but does not establish that shared training data or objectives cause the observed overlap.

rows.subject: DINOv2 and the tested language models

conditions.value: Top three modes versus full rank

relation.reason: The study measures alignment, reruns capability-trend analyses, and tests gallery density, correspondence structure, metrics and unimodal controls.

tranche.reason: Own experiments directly contest unqualified convergence and continuing capability trends, and identify metric- and data-dependent scope.

source_check.notes: The authors' coarse-overlap conclusion is supported. Joint improvement of both modalities is explicitly untested; fixed-anchor saturation establishes neither an overall asymptote nor a causal explanation from shared training data.

statements.correction: Supplement F.3 separately evaluates 25 recent base models and 20 post-trained models with the original regression fixed. Both subsets have negative predictive R² on every benchmark. These are population splits rather than controlled scale sweeps through training stages.
statements.problem: The controlled scaling gap is valid, but the description omits the study's explicit separation of base and post-trained populations.

statements.correction: Section 3.1 reports raw mutual kNN for the gallery-scale experiments. On WIT-1M the trend reappears at k=n/100 in Section 3.2.1 and Figure S2. Supplement A.2 separately examines permutation calibration when reselecting layers.
statements.problem: The returning trend is correct, but the shared conditions imply permutation calibration for this result, whereas the gallery-scale analysis reports raw mutual kNN.

statements.correction: Figure 10: DINOv2-base against 12 validation LLMs; cross-modal CKA reaches 83–92% of the vision ceiling, compared with 51–58% under RSA.
statements.problem: The 83–92% percentage is reported for the cross-modal band, not specifically for DINOv2-base–OpenLlama-3b.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Recent LLMs measured against a fixed DINOv2 vision encoder on reasoning and knowledge benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The capability-alignment trend fitted on earlier models does not extrapolate on the reported reasoning benchmarks, including ARC, GSM8K, MMLU, and LogiQA2 (R12–R15); calibrated global metrics also fail to extrapolate (R16–R17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Recent LLMs on HellaSwag and Wikitext, using mutual kNN
reader_labels.reason: The trend partially extends on these two benchmarks, but the reported R²(new) values are 0.297 and 0.489 rather than evidence of general convergence (R10–R11).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Language-model capability versus fixed DINOv2 alignment on reasoning benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Alignment does not continue the earlier capability trend for recent models on the tested reasoning benchmarks; the paper describes saturation (R12–R17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Language-model capability on HellaSwag and Wikitext, measured with mutual kNN
reader_labels.reason: A positive but partial continuation is reported on these benchmarks (R10–R11); the paper reports no continuation there with calibrated global RSA or CKA (R16–R17).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gallery density and neighborhood-size choices in cross-modal retrieval
reader_labels.reason: Fixed-small-k scores fall as galleries densify, while the n/100 setting remains stable; same-modality alignment is more stable under the same densification (R1–R7).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Choice of similarity measure and non-bijective image-text correspondences
reader_labels.reason: Mutual kNN falls as valid correspondences are added, while RSA and CKA remain in narrow reported bands on the same feature pairs (R21–R26).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Similarity measure and granularity on ImageNet
reader_labels.reason: Cross-modal alignment is much closer to the vision ceiling under CKA than under RSA, and truncated RSA peaks at three modes before declining at full rank (R18–R20).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Text-image alignment measured with fixed small-k neighborhoods as gallery density grows
reader_labels.reason: Alignment is partial and drops sharply at fixed small k, while broader proportional neighborhoods remain stable (R1–R4, R7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet cross-modal geometry across measures and caption lengths
reader_labels.reason: The study finds coarse agreement but reports lower fine-ordering agreement than the unimodal ceiling, with cross-modal scores saturating as captions lengthen (R18–R20).
